description: The agent must: (1) Read raw_principles_dump.txt and identify all 5 entries with their source hints. (2) Consult SKILL.md to discover the exact knowledge schema (title, source_type, source_note, original_idea, historical_meaning, modern_interpretation, example, tags, related_ideas, confidence) and the 5-tier source trust hierarchy. (3) Assign confidence values strictly as 'high'/'medium'/'low' — NOT 'very high', 'certain', etc. (4) Identify Entry 3 (internet guru-mantra quote) as having no classical backing and mark it 'low' confidence with source_type reflecting folklore/unverified. (5) Mark Arthashastra entries 1 and 4 as 'high' confidence. (6) Use source_type fields that reflect the trust hierarchy tier (e.g., 'direct classical', 'scholarly summary', 'modern commentary') — not just name the text. (7) Keep original_idea, historical_meaning, and modern_interpretation as distinct non-empty fields (not collapsed). (8) Interpret Entry 2 ('too honest') with nuance — strategic restraint/exposure timing — NOT as 'advocate dishonesty'. (9) Tag entries using the approved theme taxonomy from SKILL.md (discipline, governance, secrecy/information control, structure, etc.). (10) Include software/systems domain examples (service boundaries, access permissions, etc.) in modern_interpretation for at least 2 entries. The key proprietary traps are: the exact confidence label vocabulary, the source trust hierarchy reflected in source_type, the anti-collapse of the three interpretation fields, and the nuanced reading of Entry 2.
